narration.full_text: When we solve a pair of linear equations graphically, we're essentially looking at how two lines behave on a coordinate plane. The way these lines interact tells us about the nature of their solutions. Let's explore the three main possibilities. First, if the lines intersect at a single point, as you'll see on screen, this point represents the unique solution to the system. This is known as a consistent system, meaning there's exactly one solution that satisfies both equations. Next, consider what happens if the lines are parallel. If two lines are parallel, they will never intersect, no matter how far they extend. In this case, the system has no solution, because there's no common point that satisfies both equations. This type of system is called inconsistent. Finally, we have coincident lines. This occurs when both equations actually represent the exact same line. Visually, you'll see one line drawn directly over the other. Because every point on the line is common to both equations, there are infinitely many solutions. This is known as a dependent system. Understanding these graphical interpretations helps us visualize the algebraic solutions.
